newsitem.title: FRANCE: PSA Peugeot sees continued car mkt woes.
newsitem.headline: PSA Peugeot sees continued car mkt woes.

text.p: French car manufacturer PSA Peugeot Citroen announced a tumble in 1996 profit on Thursday and said the overall French car market could see sales drop by 11 to 12 percent this year.
"The fierce competition raging in Europe does not look like going away," it said in a results statement.

The statement announced a drop in net attributable profit to 734 million francs ($126.3 million) from a profit of 1.7 billion the previous year and a net dividend cut to three francs per share from five francs.

"The Western Europen car market should see overall growth of of close to two percent in 1997 but the depression of the French market since autmumn 1996 has continued unabated and sales could recede by 11-12 percent over the year," it said.

As far as Peugeot itself was concerned, the company said: "Nevertheless, bolstered by the success of its car range, notably in the light commercial vehicles sector, PSA Peugeot Citroen sales should meet the target gains which the group has set itself".
Operating profit tumbled to 1.675 billion francs ($288.3 million) from 3.751 billion francs, while sales had risen to 172.668 billion francs from 164,248 billion the preceding year, it said.
